title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2611.14504v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. translated_title: 分子相互作用基础模型中涌现的生物能力
translated_abstract: 在大规模无标注语料库上训练的基础模型会发展出涌现能力，即超越其训练目标的任务。我们将这一范式扩展至多模态生物学领域，提出了Bonbon——一个在约3.2万亿个蛋白质-配体配对序列token上训练的分子相互作用基础模型。从单一的表示空间出发，Bonbon在层次化的分辨率水平上展现出三种零样本涌现能力：功能层面（作用机制）、残基层面（结合位点定位，包括正构位点与变构位点的区分）以及键层面（共价与非共价相互作用的判别）。这三种能力均可泛化至分布外的复合物。Bonbon仅通过蛋白质-配体序列进行训练，未使用任何任务特定的监督，也未使用结构坐标。我们开展了从4200万到16亿参数共六个模型规模的受控缩放实验；所评估的每一项能力均表现出急剧的跃升（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了仅凭蛋白质-配体序列训练、无需任务监督和结构坐标的分子相互作用基础模型Bonbon，其单一表示空间在功能、残基和键三个层次涌现出零样本生物能力，并能泛化到分布外复合物。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces Bonbon, a molecular interaction foundation model trained solely on paired protein-ligand sequences without task supervision or structural coordinates, whose single representation space exhibits emergent zero-shot biological capabilities at the functional, residue, and bond levels that generalize to out-of-distribution complexes.
